content.comment_body: Hello, I'm interested in how you managed to control the (On/Off) Days from the web server. I'm trying to operate an output using a weekly timer and wish to edit the Days and Times directly from the web interface. Any suggestions or guidance would be greatly appreciated!

I directly write to the V-Bits of the [product_name]. For example: Sunday = V0.0, Monday = V0.1, ... Friday = V0.5, Saturday = V0.6. Then I transfer the group of V-Bits (V0.0 to V0.7) via Parameter VM Mapping to the parameter 'Weekday1' of the weekly timer. That's the whole process.
Hello. You might want to check this video: [url]

Thank you very much, I've got it working now. But I ran into an issue where the analog inputs on the web interface show values as (16#Hour) (16#Minute) instead of just (Hour) (Minute). How can I make it display only the regular hour and minute values? I believe this topic has been covered before, but I'm still unsure how to solve it.
Thank you so much, this is incredibly helpful!
Thank you, you really helped me out!

analysis.insight_summary: Users want to manipulate weekly timer schedules, specifically days and times, for outputs directly via the web interface using [product_name] and its web editor. The main difficulty involves configuring the interface for clear and straightforward editing of day/time settings, especially the need to display time values in standard hour/minute format instead of hexadecimal. Community members provided solutions involving input mapping, referenced earlier resources, and the initial goal was met, though one detail about time formatting still needs clarification.
analysis.user_expectations: Users aim to edit weekly timer days and times easily and directly in the web interface, expecting intuitive controls and clear display of values in standard hour/minute format, rather than hexadecimal.
